thread:
Alex C.: Heads-up — started seeing an uptick in partial WS frames from prod region eu-west-1 around 08:12 UTC. Clients report truncated responses mid-stream. Anyone already digging? :thinking:
Mira P.: saw that on the streaming dashboard. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/streaming/ws-chunk-health — error rate for chunked responses jumped from ~0.4% to ~6% between 08:10-08:15. Looks correlated with a deploy in the eu pool. :eyes:
Samir: can confirm. digging into logs now. quick grep for "partial_frame" shows a bunch of these in the runtime logs:
```
2026-03-12T08:11:43.123Z INFO ws_conn=abc123 partial_frame detected seq=927 client=app-42 reason=remote-eof
2026-03-12T08:11:43.124Z WARN  kv_cache miss seq=927
2026-03-12T08:12:01.998Z INFO ws_conn=def456 partial_frame detected seq=12 client=browser-7 reason=timeout
```
You can run:
```
kubectl logs -l app=redwood-runtime -n prod --since=30m | rg "partial_frame" | head -n 50
```
Lucy (sre): interesting — I see the deploy Mira mentioned. @samir can you check if the new runtime change touched the chunking codepath / conn keepalive timings? Also pinging @alex for the PR that rolled the change.
Samir: yep the PR is #4523 — I added an optimization for early flush on partial prefixes. It passed unit tests but maybe edge-case with mobile clients. I'm rolling back the change in a hotfix branch now.
Alex C.: thanks. While Samir rolls back, can we also look at traces for a few affected request IDs? Jaeger query: service=runtime and tag ws_conn=abc123 (or use /trace?q=ws_conn:abc123). That should show where the TCP socket closed relative to send() calls.
Mira P.: also putting a quick alert adjustment suggestion: current alert "ws_partial_rate > 1% for 5m" is too noisy post-deploy. Propose: change to ">3% for 10m" and add an annotation linking to the deploy tag so on-call can triage. Thoughts?
Lucy (sre): +1 on adding deploy tag annotation. But I'd prefer threshold bump only for eu regions until we confirm global impact. Suggested PromQL tweak:
```
sum by(region) (rate(ws_partial_frames_total[10m])) / sum by(region) (rate(ws_frames_total[10m])) > 0.03
```
and alert if region=="eu-west-1" OR global > 0.05
```
Samir: rolling back now. once rollback is live I'll post here with the new pod images. also will open a small follow-up PR to add an integration test that simulates slow flush clients.
alerts-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0312-042 — "Partial WS frames spike (eu-west-1)" — assigned to eng-runtime oncall. https://incidents.redwood.com/INC-2026-0312-042
Alex C.: thanks @alerts-bot. Samir when the rollback is up, can you drop the pod image and the rollback commit hash here? I'll follow up with a quick postmortem note and a short blameless RCA.
Samir: rollback deployed. new image: runtime:v2026-03-12-hotfix-7 hash=ab9f2d. Monitoring now — partial frame rate back to ~0.5% after ~3 minutes. Will keep an eye for 30m.
Mira P.: confirmed on Grafana — curve trending down. I'm going to tune the alert to the regional rule Lucy suggested and add the deploy tag. PR to alerting infra in a sec.
Alex C.: great. small follow-up: Samir can you add a short comment on PR #4523 describing the edge-case and linking to this thread so we don't reintroduce it? also pinging @lucy for any runbook updates.
Lucy (sre): will add a one-liner to the streaming runbook about "partial_frame" triage steps and the jaeger/grep commands. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Samir: will do all that. also @alex FYI I requested a quick review from @mira on the integration test PR.
Alex C.: perfect. closing loop — final check in 30m and then I'll mark the incident as resolved if steady. "
